mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% may indicate monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs rise and consumer spending decreases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth combined with high inflation may lead to expectations of tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of periods when GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL are both high, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate may lead to decreased liquidity and negative S&P 500 returns as investors become risk-averse.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS increases by 0.2pp, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales signals strong consumer demand, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as companies experience higher revenues and earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS increases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Strong growth in non-farm employment indicates a robust labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment combined with rising federal funds rates may signal a tightening labor market and increased borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate margins are squeezed.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE is low and FEDFUNDS are rising, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production in a late-cycle expansion may indicate an overheating economy, leading to expectations of a slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns as growth falters.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is above 105, this hypothesis is rejected.
